messages:
Maya C.: Heads-up — Acme customer's on call just escalated a pretty nasty reconnect bug for streaming (SSE). They see duplicate completions after a client reconnect and sometimes partial trailing chunks. Billing counts tokens twice. Repro steps attached.

Diego S.: Thanks — can you paste the session headers + sample flow? Also curious if they're doing short-lived session tokens or rotating auth.

Maya C.: Paste from customer:

```
Client opens SSE with headers:
  Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-rotating
  X-Resume-Token: r=eyJzZXNzaW9uIjoiMTIzNCIsInNlcS... (base64)
  X-Client-Id: acme-frontend-42

Server replies (200 OK, event: resume_ok)
--- stream ---
```

On reconnect (network blip) client retries with same X-Resume-Token and receives the last few tokens again, plus a fresh generation appended. They report duplicates in outputs (same text repeated) and partial outputs when the client dropped mid-completion. Billing shows 2x tokens for duplicates.

Kevin L.: Hmm — do they include an idempotency/generation id on create requests? We support `x-generation-id` on the creation path but streaming resume currently relies solely on the resume token and an in-memory last_ack seq per connection.

acme-integ: Confirmed: we do not set any explicit generation id from the client — it's all server-side. We can't change client quickly.

Anya R.: From infra perspective, I think root cause is: resume token is short (rotating per minute) and when the client reconnects with an expired/rotated Authorization header, our proxy will create a new server-side session and replay the last cached buffers as part of resume. If the original server had already flushed the completion to downstream and incremented billing counters, the replay becomes a duplicate generation.

Jen H.: Can you paste logs showing billing increment and replay? Any request IDs we can tie together?

Maya C.: Logs (redacted ids):
```
[2026-02-08T12:03:01Z] conn_id=abc123 session_id=sess-9a start_generation gen_id=g-87
[2026-02-08T12:03:05Z] conn_id=abc123 completion_sent bytes=345 tokens=58 billed=true
[2026-02-08T12:03:07Z] conn_id=abc123 network_error -> client disconnected
[2026-02-08T12:03:09Z] conn_id=def456 session_id=sess-9a resume_token=r-xxxxx matched_cache=true
[2026-02-08T12:03:09Z] conn_id=def456 replay_chunk gen_id=g-87 tokens=58 billed=false? <-- TODO
[2026-02-08T12:03:10Z] conn_id=def456 start_generation gen_id=g-91
[2026-02-08T12:03:12Z] conn_id=def456 completion_sent bytes=540 tokens=89 billed=true
```

Customer says they were billed twice for the 58-token generation. Our logs are inconsistent: replay_chunk shows `billed=false?` but billing service still shows charge. Looks like billing increments on finalization not on `billed` flag; there is a race.

Diego S.: Repro steps from Acme (condensed):
1) open SSE -> get stream
2) request completion (no client gen id)
3) wait until partial output arrives (first 30 tokens)
4) drop network (simulate wifi off)
5) reconnect within ~10s with same resume token
6) client replays resume -> sees last 30 tokens plus the rest -> sometimes the remainder is replayed and server treats it as a new completion

Kevin L.: Potential mitigations:
- Short term: On replay, do not re-invoke billing increment for chunks that match an existing generation_id in our session store. That requires keeping a small LRU of recently finalized gen_ids for the session.
- Medium: Add `X-Client-Generation-Id` header support and prefer client-supplied gen_id for dedupe. Encourage clients to set a UUID per user-visible generation.
- Long term: Change resume semantics so replay sends only until last_ack_seq and then expects client to request continuation; avoid implicit new generation creation on resume.

Anya R.: For short term we can add a hotfix: session store keeps `finalized_gen_ids: [g-87,...]` for TTL 5m. On replay, if we detect replay_chunk with gen_id in finalized list, we drop billing hook. That should stop double-charges. Might need contract with billing team to retrofix any already doubled charges.

sre-rotations (@jen): We should also consider tokenization-edge duplicates: if replayed chunk boundaries differ, identical content might not match gen_id checks. Maybe add content-hash dedupe fallback: hash of the first N tokens of a generation.

acme-integ: One more data point — when we reconnect with different Authorization (rotated key) but same resume token, proxy created a new internal session ID (conn_id changed) but session_id was same. So session_id is persisted in resume token; conn_id is ephemeral.

Diego S.: Action items proposed:
- eng-runtime (Kevin): implement temporary finalized_gen_ids TTL-5m dedupe + billing guard (priority P0) — small change in session lifecycle.
- eng-sre (Anya/Jen): monitor for replay_rate and billing anomalies, add alert if replayed_token_count > 1% of streams in an hour.
- support/cs (Maya/Diego): Contact Acme, explain hotfix plan and offer one-off refund for duplicate charges while we roll fix.
- product: decide if we want to surface `X-Client-Generation-Id` in API docs and SDKs.

Kevin L.: I'll start a PR for the hotfix branch — proto sketch:

```
// session struct
session.finalized_gen_ids = LRU(cache_size=64, ttl=300s)

on_completion(gen_id, content_hash):
  session.finalized_gen_ids.add(gen_id)
  emit_billing_event(gen_id)

on_resume_replay(gen_id, chunk_hash):
  if session.finalized_gen_ids.contains(gen_id) or session.hash_seen(chunk_hash):
    drop_billing()
    mark_chunk_as_duplicate
  else:
    forward_chunk()
```

Will also add telemetry counters `replay.duplicate_dropped` and `replay.unexpected_new_generation`.

Anya R.: We need a deploy-safe feature flag gated rollout for this. Also ensure this doesn't break legal/compliance metrics that expect billing events to be emitted on every `completion_sent` log line.

Maya C.: Customer-facing message drafted:
"We're investigating a streaming resume issue that can cause duplicated text and duplicate billing when network reconnections occur. We're preparing an immediate server-side fix that prevents double-billing for recently finalized completions. We'll follow up with an update and a refund for affected tokens."

acme-integ: Appreciate the quick response. One ask: can you provide a reproducible script we can run locally to demonstrate the fix before you roll to prod?

Kevin L.: I'll attach a small curl+node repro (will post once PR is up). Short term customers can also add client-side gen ids. For longer term, let's spec resume window and add fields `resume_seq` and `client_generation_id` to the streaming handshake.

Jen H.: I'll add an incident postmortem template item to track root-cause, timeline, customer impact, and follow-ups. @everyone please add any logs or customer-facing notes to this thread.

session-bot: deploy-check queued for hotfix branch. CI: unit tests + integration replay-test.

Maya C.: Thanks — will keep Acme updated. Marking high priority, billing involved :money_with_wings:.
